chunks: From him, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When two or three men kill one man, if his guardians want to execute them all, they must pay back the excess blood money; otherwise they take the blood money of their companion (the killed).

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاء: Awliya' — the guardians or next of kin (heirs) of the murdered person who hold the right to demand qisas or accept diya
key_terms.دِيَة: Diya — blood money, the monetary compensation paid in lieu of retaliation
key_terms.فَضْل الدِّيَات: The excess blood money — when multiple killers are executed for one killing, the families of the excess killers must receive compensation
key_terms.قِصَاص: Qisas — the right of retaliation, allowing the victim's heirs to demand execution of the killer(s)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when multiple men jointly kill one person?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the question of group liability in homicide cases. When multiple perpetrators jointly kill a single victim, the victim's next of kin (awliya') have the right to execute all killers (qisas), but only if they first compensate the other killers' families for the excess blood money (diya). Alternatively, they may forgo execution and simply receive the standard diya for their slain relative. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that qisas (retaliation) must not result in disproportionate harm to third parties.
